title: How Fear Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore how fear works, starting with a personal scare story from Josh's teenage years. They define fear as a chain reaction in the brain ending in the fight-or-flight response, and describe the autonomic nervous system and the brain regions involved (thalamus, sensory cortex, hippocampus, amygdala, hypothalamus). They explain Joseph LeDoux's low road and high road pathways, the role of emotions as survival motivators, Paul Ekman's six basic emotions, Darwin's snake-at-the-zoo experiment, John Watson's Little Albert conditioning experiment, common fears and phobia categories, culturally bound fears such as taijin kyofusho, fear extinction and drug research involving NMDA and a tuberculosis antibiotic, a suspension bridge experiment on arousal, and tips for overcoming fear. The episode closes with listener mail from a listener in Kazakhstan.
topics: low road high road fear response

entities.name: Bob Newhart Show episode Flying the Unfriendly Skies

segments.title: Opening banter and Josh's closet scare story
segments.summary: Hosts plug their Twitter, Facebook, and an old article on eyes in paintings. Josh tells a story about being startled by his father opening a closet door when he was a teenager, and recounts scaring a roommate with screwed-in lightbulbs.

segments.title: Defining fear and the brain's fight-or-flight pathway
segments.summary: Fear is defined as a brain chain reaction starting from a stimulus and ending in fight or flight, an autonomic response run by the autonomic nervous system. The hosts describe the roles of the thalamus, sensory cortex, hippocampus, amygdala, and hypothalamus.

segments.title: Low road and high road fear responses
segments.summary: Joseph LeDoux's two pathways for fear are explained using an example of a rattling door. The low road is a fast, crude response, while the high road involves the sensory cortex and hippocampus to give context. Both run at once and end at the hypothalamus.

segments.title: Emotions as survival motivators and Darwin's snake experiment
segments.summary: Emotions are described as survival-based motivators, with Paul Ekman's six basic emotions from the 1970s. Using a caveman example, fear is linked to natural selection. Darwin's book on expression of emotions and his experiment with a puff adder behind glass at the zoo are discussed.

segments.title: Anticipatory fear and the Little Albert experiment
segments.summary: The hosts discuss anticipatory fear such as fear of flying, then John Watson's 1920s Little Albert experiment in which a baby was conditioned to fear white rats using a loud noise. The hosts note Albert's fate is unknown and Watson was fired after an affair.

segments.title: Common fears, phobia categories, and cultural fears
segments.summary: Phobias are grouped into agoraphobia, social phobia, and specific phobia. A 2005 poll of US teenagers lists top fears, including terrorist attacks, spiders, and death. Universal fears such as snakes, spiders, and rats are discussed, along with regionally and culturally bound fears like hurricanes versus tornadoes and taijin kyofusho.

segments.title: Fear extinction, exposure therapy, and drug research
segments.summary: Fear extinction is described as the reverse of conditioning, with exposure therapy as the main method. Research suggests the extinction memory forms in the amygdala and is stored in the medial prefrontal cortex. A protein called NMDA is linked to extinction, and a tuberculosis antibiotic that promotes it was tested in rats. The hosts also note the health effects of chronic fear.

segments.title: Arousal and fear experiment on suspension bridges
segments.summary: Arthur Aron's experiment is described in which men crossed a stable or shaky suspension bridge and then met an attractive assistant. More men on the shaky bridge later called her, which the hosts link to the thrill of fear and arousal. Statistics on about nineteen million Americans with fear-related mental illness are mentioned.

segments.title: Eight tips for overcoming fear
segments.summary: The hosts go through tips from a Prevention magazine article, including learning about the feared thing, taking baby steps, talking about it, avoiding mind games like imagining the audience naked, and seeking help for irrational fears.

segments.title: Listener mail from Kazakhstan
segments.summary: A listener in Astana, Kazakhstan, writes that he listens to the podcast on his commute and studied in the United States and Canada. The hosts read the email and thank him.

segments.title: Sign-off and promo
segments.summary: The hosts ask listeners to share their fears by email and promote the Stuff from the Future video podcast.
